newsitem.title: USA: Financial firms lend backing to IRA expansion.
newsitem.headline: Financial firms lend backing to IRA expansion.

text.p: Wall Street financial firms, bankers and realtors Wednesday applauded a bipartisan Senate proposal to expand individual retirement savings accounts, saying it would encourage personal savings.

At a Capitol Hill news conference, Senate Finance Committee chairman William Roth, a Delaware Republican, Senate Democratic Whip John Breaux of Louisiana and other lawmakers said their plan would permit all taxpayers to have fully deductible IRA accounts by 2001.
Now, only those not covered by other pension plans and whose income is below $40,000 a year can contribute $2,000 to a tax-free IRA account.
Their plan would create a new IRA-plus account where contributions would not be tax deductible but the interest accumulated would be tax-free at retirement.
"Our tax laws today still discourage too many Americans from saving," Roth said.
While the exact cost to the Treasury of the IRA expansion has not been calculated, the tax reduction from a similar bill offered last year was valued at nearly $30 billion over seven years.

The legislation would also allow penalty-free withdrawals for first-time home purchases, a move the National Association of Realtors said would solve the problem entry-level buyers face when they cannot come up with a downpayment and closing costs on a home.
To that end, the bill would permit parents and grandparents to tap their own IRA accounts without a tax pentalty to help children and grandchildren with home purchases.
The 10 percent tax penalty on early withdrawals would also be waived to pay education expenses or to cover long term unemployment once government benefits have run out.
Senate Democratic leaders Tuesday unveiled a list of legislative priorities which included raising the size of IRA contributions to a maximum of $2,500 a year.
